plan.goal: Evaluate the UX of the Stratabox single-page marketing site, focusing on the interactive 'Live Block Builder' demo, SDK documentation usability, and mobile responsiveness of complex UI elements.
plan.summary: The run will treat index.html as a multi-section application. It begins with global navigation and hero validation, moves to deep interaction testing of the drag-and-drop content builder, verifies the developer-facing SDK tabs and search filters, and concludes with a rigorous mobile viewport check to address known tap-target risks.
assumptions: The site is a Single Page Application (SPA) style landing page where 'Pricing', 'Product', etc., are scroll anchors rather than separate HTML files.
The 'Start free' and 'Sign in' buttons likely trigger modals or external redirects not fully captured in the static prescan.
The 'Live Block Builder' relies on client-side JS for state management (drag-and-drop, auto-save simulation).
risk_hotspots: Builder Drag-and-Drop: HTML5 DnD often fails on touch devices or has poor accessibility.
SDK Copy Buttons: Clipboard API permissions can fail silently in local file contexts.
Mobile Navigation: Prescan indicates numerous small tap targets (<44px) in the header and builder controls.
Integrations Search: Live filtering logic may have edge cases with special characters or empty states.

phases.title: Global Nav & Hero Validation
phases.objective: Verify sticky header behavior, smooth scrolling to anchors, and initial hero state.
key_checks: Click each nav link (Product, Builder, SDKs, Pricing) to verify scroll-to-anchor behavior.
Validate 'Start free' and 'Book a demo' CTA visibility and hover states.
Observe the hero 'editor-vs-live-preview' split panel for the periodic block-swap animation.
exit_criteria: All nav links scroll to correct sections.
Hero animation cycles at least once.

phases.title: Interactive Builder Stress Test
phases.objective: Deeply exercise the 'Live Block Builder' demo to validate drag-and-drop, editing, and state feedback.
key_checks: Drag a block (e.g., 'Callout') to reorder it; verify visual drop indicator and final position.
Type into the 'New section heading' input; verify real-time update in the Live Preview pane.
Click '+ Paragraph' or '+ Image' to add a new block; verify it appears in both panes.
Wait for the 'debounced auto-save' status indicator to update (e.g., 'saved' vs 'saving').
exit_criteria: Successful reordering of at least 2 blocks.

phases.title: Developer Experience (SDKs & Integrations)
phases.objective: Validate the usability of code snippets and the integrations discovery flow.
key_checks: Switch between SDK tabs (JS, Python, Ruby, curl); verify syntax highlighting updates.
Click the 'Copy' button on a snippet; check for toast notification or visual feedback.
Type a query in the 'Search 24 visible integrations' input; verify grid filtering and count update.
Clear the search input; verify all integrations return.
exit_criteria: Search filter successfully hid non-matching items.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Accessibility
phases.objective: Repeat critical checks on mobile viewport to address prescan warnings about small tap targets.
key_checks: Attempt to use the Builder drag-and-drop on touch/mobile emulation (high risk of failure).
Check if the sticky nav collapses into a hamburger menu or remains usable.
Verify text readability in the split-pane editor on narrow screens.
exit_criteria: Builder usability assessment completed (even if unusable, that is a finding).

coverage_targets.pages: 100% of index.html sections (Hero, Builder, SDKs, Integrations, Footer)
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all builder controls (add, delete, reorder, edit) and all SDK tabs
coverage_targets.mobile: Full pass on mobile viewport for layout integrity and touch targets

notes: Prescan identified ~10 small tap targets in the header and builder controls; prioritize checking these in Phase 4.
Since this is a local file system run, clipboard permissions for the 'Copy' button might be restricted by the browser; note if this prevents testing.
The 'Pricing' section is described as a 'teaser' in the summary; verify if it links out or expands.
